notice.weekend.title: Service Canada agents answer on weekdays.
notice.weekend.body: They’re available 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. your local time, Monday to Friday. Rather not wait? Ask online and an officer will call you back within 2 business days.
notice.abroad.title: Calling from outside Canada and the U.S.?
notice.abroad.body: International numbers come first where the department lists one. Hours are shown in your time. For lines listed in “local time”, we’ve assumed Eastern time, so check the official page.

fraud.steps.title: If you’ve been scammed
fraud.steps.bank.title: Contact your bank or financial institution
fraud.steps.bank.detail: Report it to the institution that sent the money. If your identity was used, also alert Equifax and TransUnion.
fraud.steps.police.title: Report it to your local police
fraud.steps.police.detail: Ask for a file number and keep it for later.
fraud.steps.report.title: Tell the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre
fraud.steps.report.detail: Online any time, or by phone on weekdays. Report even a suspected scam: every report gives police what they need to stop scammers.
fraud.recovery.title: Scammers often come back promising to recover your money.
fraud.recovery.body: Never pay anyone to get money back. Share any updates with the Anti-Fraud Centre, your bank and the police.
tryFirst.title: Try online first: your CRA account, chat and automated lines are often faster

urgent.subtitle.suspected: How to check it, and who to tell
suspect.signs.title: The CRA will never
suspect.signs.threats: Threaten to arrest or deport you, or put you in prison
suspect.signs.pay: Demand immediate payment by gift card, prepaid credit card, cryptocurrency or Interac e‑Transfer
suspect.signs.refund: Send you a refund by e‑Transfer or text message
suspect.signs.fee: Charge a fee to speak with an agent
suspect.signs.voicemail: Ask for personal or financial information in a voicemail or email
suspect.signs.note: Caller ID can be faked. A real CRA agent may ask for your SIN to confirm who you are, so when in doubt, hang up and call the CRA yourself.
suspect.steps.title: What to do now
suspect.steps.verify.title: Hang up and check with the CRA yourself
suspect.steps.verify.detail: Sign in to your CRA account, or call the number listed on canada.ca. Never call back a number the caller gave you.
suspect.steps.report.title: Report it, even if you lost nothing
suspect.steps.report.detail: Tell the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre online, any time, or by phone on weekdays. Every report helps police stop scammers.
suspect.steps.paid.title: Only if you paid or shared details
suspect.steps.paid.detail: Call your bank or financial institution right away, then your local police for a file number. If they got your CRA sign-in or SIN, tell the CRA too: by phone, it can protect your account during the call.
suspect.steps.paid.link: Report it to the CRA online
line.hope.langs: English and French, and Cree, Ojibway or Inuktitut on request

notice.us.title: Calling from the United States?
notice.us.body: The CRA, EI and CPP/OAS toll-free numbers are listed for Canada and the United States. Hours are shown in your time: lines that run on “local time” follow your own clock.
